Anatomy-01.question: ১) Cells having no mitochondria
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is RBC (red blood cell). Mature red blood cells lack mitochondria to maximize oxygen transport and avoid using the oxygen they carry.

Key points:

  • Mature RBC:

    • No mitochondria

    • No nucleus

    • Generate ATP through anaerobic glycolysis

    • Lifespan ≈ 120 days

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Neutrophil → Contains mitochondria.

  • Neuron → Contains numerous mitochondria due to high energy demand.

  • Hepatocyte → Rich in mitochondria for metabolic functions.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Cell without mitochondria = Mature RBC

Exam pearl:
Mature erythrocyte lacks mitochondria.

Anatomy-01.question: ২) Chromatid is formed during-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Prophase. During prophase of mitosis, chromatin condenses and becomes visible as duplicated chromosomes, each consisting of two sister chromatids joined at the centromere.

Cell cycle sequence:

  • Interphase (S phase) → DNA replication occurs → sister chromatids are formed

  • Prophase → Chromosomes become visible due to condensation

  • Metaphase → Chromosomes align at the equator

  • Anaphase → Sister chromatids separate

  • Telophase → New nuclei form

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Anaphase → Sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles.

  • Metaphase → Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.

  • Telophase → Chromosomes decondense and nuclear envelope reforms.

High-yield cell cycle recall:

S phase → DNA duplication → sister chromatids formed
Prophase → visible chromosomes

Exam pearl:
Chromatid formation begins after DNA replication in S phase and becomes visible during prophase.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩) Transitional epithelium prevents urine from leaking of the bladder due to -
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is tight junction. Transitional epithelium (urothelium) prevents leakage of urine by tight junctions between superficial umbrella cells, forming a highly impermeable barrier.

Key points:

  • Tight junctions prevent passage of:

    • Urine

    • Water

    • Solutes

  • Uroplakins on umbrella cells also contribute to urine impermeability.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Glycocalyx → Provides surface protection and cell recognition, not the main sealing mechanism.

  • Hemidesmosome → Anchors epithelial cells to the basement membrane.

  • Gap junction → Allows communication between adjacent cells, not prevention of leakage.

High-yield histology recall:

Transitional epithelium impermeability → Tight junction + uroplakin

Exam pearl:
Urinary bladder barrier = Tight junctions between umbrella cells.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪) Which is functions of microvilli-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is absorption. Microvilli are finger-like projections of the apical surface of epithelial cells that increase surface area for absorption.

Key points:

  • Present mainly in:

    • Small intestine → nutrient absorption

    • Proximal renal tubules → reabsorption

  • Contain actin filaments

  • Form the brush border in absorptive cells

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Neurotransmission → Function of synapses and neurons.

  • Collagen formation → Function of fibroblasts.

  • Secretory activities → Mainly associated with glandular cells and organelles like rough ER and Golgi apparatus.

High-yield histology recall:

Microvilli = Increased surface area → Absorption

Exam pearl:
Main function of microvilli = absorption.

Anatomy-01.question: ৫) Zonulae occludens is another name of
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is tight junctions. Zonula occludens is the Latin name for tight junctions, which form an impermeable seal between adjacent epithelial cells.

Key points:

  • Located at the apical part of lateral cell membranes

  • Prevents movement of substances between cells (paracellular pathway)

  • Maintains epithelial barrier function

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Gap junctions → Allow communication and exchange of ions/small molecules between cells.

  • Desmosome → Provides strong cell-to-cell adhesion.

  • Hemidesmosome → Anchors epithelial cells to the basement membrane.

High-yield histology recall:

Zonula occludens = Tight junction
Zonula adherens = Adherens junction
Macula adherens = Desmosome

Exam pearl:
Zonula occludens is another name for tight junction

Anatomy-01.question: ৬) Which one is the major constituent of plasma membrane?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is protein. Proteins are the major constituent of the plasma membrane by mass and are responsible for most membrane functions.

Components of plasma membrane:

  • Protein (~50% by mass) → Transport, receptors, enzymes, cell signalling

  • Phospholipid (~40%) → Forms the lipid bilayer framework

  • Cholesterol → Maintains membrane fluidity and stability

  • Carbohydrate → Cell recognition and glycocalyx formation

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Phospholipid → Major structural component but not the major constituent by mass.

  • Cholesterol → Regulates fluidity, but present in smaller amounts.

  • Carbohydrate → Minor component attached to proteins/lipids.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Major constituent of plasma membrane (by mass) = Protein
Basic structural framework = Phospholipid bilayer

Exam pearl:
Plasma membrane = Lipid bilayer + proteins; proteins are the major functional component.

৮) Primary ossification centre is in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is diaphysis. The primary ossification centre develops in the shaft (diaphysis) of a long bone during endochondral ossification.

Key points:

  • Primary ossification centre → Diaphysis (appears during fetal life)

  • Secondary ossification centres → Epiphysis (usually appear after birth)

  • Epiphyseal plate → Responsible for longitudinal bone growth

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epiphysis → Site of secondary ossification centre.

  • Epiphyseal plate of cartilage → Site of growth, not primary ossification.

  • Metaphysis → Region between diaphysis and epiphysis; contains growth plate.

High-yield embryology recall:

Primary ossification centre = Diaphysis
Secondary ossification centre = Epiphysis

Exam pearl:
Long bone ossification starts in the diaphysis.

১৬) Most abundant constituent of bone matrix
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is calcium hydroxyapatite. Calcium hydroxyapatite is the most abundant inorganic constituent of bone matrix and provides hardness and strength to bone.

Composition of bone matrix:

  • Inorganic component (~65%)

    • Calcium hydroxyapatite → major mineral component

  • Organic component (~35%)

    • Type I collagen → provides tensile strength

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Bicarbonate → Present in small amounts as a bone mineral component.

  • Citrate → Present in minor amounts.

  • Magnesium → Trace mineral component.

High-yield bone recall:

Bone matrix:

  • Most abundant inorganic component → Calcium hydroxyapatite

  • Most abundant organic component → Type I collagen

Exam pearl:
Bone hardness = Calcium hydroxyapatite.

Anatomy-01.question: ১৭) Intramembranous ossification mainly occurs in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is flat bone. Intramembranous ossification occurs directly from mesenchymal tissue and mainly forms flat bones of the skull and facial bones.

Examples of intramembranous ossification:

  • Flat bones of skull

  • Facial bones

  • Mandible

  • Clavicle

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Long bone → Mainly develops by endochondral ossification.

  • Short bone → Mainly develops by endochondral ossification.

  • Sesamoid bone → Develops by endochondral ossification.

High-yield embryology recall:

Intramembranous ossification → Flat bones
Endochondral ossification → Long bones

Exam pearl:
Skull flat bones are formed by intramembranous ossification.

Anatomy-01.question: ১৮) Shortest phase of cell division
১৯) Cell division occurs in which phase of cell cycle?
২০) How many daughter cells are formed during meiosis?
২১) Gap junctions abundant in
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is muscular tissue. Gap junctions are abundant in cardiac muscle and smooth muscle, where they allow rapid communication and coordinated contraction between cells.

Key points:

  • Gap junctions:

    • Form channels between adjacent cells

    • Allow passage of ions and small molecules

    • Enable electrical coupling

Examples:

  • Cardiac muscle → Synchronised contraction of myocardium

  • Smooth muscle → Coordinated contraction

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epithelial tissue → Has gap junctions but less abundant compared with muscle.

  • Connective tissue → Few gap junctions.

  • Nervous tissue → Chemical synapses are the main communication method.

High-yield histology recall:

Gap junction abundant → Cardiac muscle
Desmosome → Mechanical strength
Tight junction → Prevent leakage

Exam pearl:
Most prominent gap junctions are found in cardiac muscle.

Anatomy-01.question: ২২) Holocrine gland
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is sebaceous gland. Holocrine glands release their secretion by complete destruction of the secretory cells.

Examples of secretion types:

  • Holocrine gland → Sebaceous gland

    • Whole cell disintegrates to release sebum

  • Apocrine gland → Mammary gland (lipid secretion portion)

  • Merocrine gland → Sweat gland, salivary gland

  • Goblet cell → Unicellular mucous-secreting gland (merocrine type)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Goblet cell → Merocrine secretion.

  • Mammary glands → Mainly apocrine (milk fat secretion).

  • Sweat glands → Mainly merocrine (eccrine).

High-yield histology recall:

Holocrine = Sebaceous gland
Apocrine = Mammary gland
Merocrine = Sweat gland

Exam pearl:
Complete cell destruction for secretion → Sebaceous gland.

Anatomy-01.question: ২৩) Phagocytosis of ECM components and debris done by
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is macrophages. Macrophages are professional phagocytic cells that remove extracellular matrix (ECM) components, dead cells, and cellular debris by phagocytosis.

Key points:

  • Derived from monocytes

  • Functions:

    • Phagocytosis of debris and pathogens

    • Antigen presentation

    • Cytokine secretion

    • Tissue repair regulation

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Fibroblasts → Produce ECM components (collagen, elastin, ground substance), not mainly phagocytic.

  • Lymphocytes → Responsible for immune responses but not phagocytosis.

  • Eosinophils → Involved in parasitic defense and allergic reactions.

High-yield histology recall:

ECM debris removal → Macrophages
ECM production → Fibroblasts

Exam pearl:
Main phagocytic cell in connective tissue = Macrophage.

Anatomy-01.question: ২৪) Example of loose connective tissue-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is lamina propria. Lamina propria is a typical example of loose connective tissue containing loosely arranged collagen fibres, elastic fibres, fibroblasts, and abundant ground substance.

Examples:

  • Loose connective tissue:

    • Lamina propria of mucous membranes

    • Areolar tissue beneath epithelium

    • Around blood vessels and nerves

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Dermis of skin → Dense irregular connective tissue.

  • Aponeuroses → Dense regular connective tissue.

  • Corneal stroma → Dense regular connective tissue (highly organized collagen).

High-yield histology recall:

Loose CT → Lamina propria (areolar tissue)
Dense irregular CT → Dermis
Dense regular CT → Tendon, ligament, aponeurosis

Exam pearl:
Classic example of loose connective tissue = Lamina propria.

Anatomy-01.question: ২৫) Example of Hyaline cartilage-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is foetal skeleton. Hyaline cartilage forms the temporary skeleton of the fetus and acts as a template for endochondral ossification.

Examples of hyaline cartilage:

  • Foetal skeleton

  • Articular cartilage

  • Costal cartilage

  • Tracheal and bronchial cartilage

  • Nasal cartilage

The other options are incorrect because:

  • External ear → Elastic cartilage.

  • Auditory tube → Elastic cartilage.

  • Meniscus → Fibrocartilage.

High-yield histology recall:

Hyaline cartilage → Foetal skeleton, articular cartilage, costal cartilage
Elastic cartilage → Ear, auditory tube, epiglottis
Fibrocartilage → Intervertebral disc, meniscus

Exam pearl:
Temporary fetal skeleton = Hyaline cartilage.

Anatomy-01.question: ২৬) Criteria of meiosis excludes
Anatomy-01.option4: Daughter cells are genetically identical to parent cell

Anatomy-01.question: ২৭) Tissue with abundant amount of extracellular matrix
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is connective tissue. Connective tissue has abundant extracellular matrix (ECM), which provides structural support, binding, and protection.

Key points:

  • ECM consists of:

    • Ground substance

    • Protein fibres (collagen, elastic, reticular)

    • Tissue fluid

  • Examples:

    • Bone

    • Cartilage

    • Blood

    • Fibrous connective tissue

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Epithelial tissue → Cells are tightly packed with minimal extracellular matrix.

  • Muscle tissue → Mainly composed of contractile cells with little ECM.

  • Nervous tissue → Mainly neurons and supporting glial cells with limited ECM.

High-yield histology recall:

Abundant extracellular matrix = Connective tissue
Closely packed cells = Epithelium

Exam pearl:
Connective tissue is defined by abundant extracellular matrix.

৩৪) Which cell stores neutral fats?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is adipocyte. Adipocytes are specialized connective tissue cells that store neutral fats (triglycerides) in large lipid droplets.

Key points:

  • Adipocyte functions:

    • Storage of neutral fat (triglyceride)

    • Energy reserve

    • Insulation

    • Endocrine function (e.g., leptin secretion)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Plasma cell → Produces antibodies (immunoglobulins).

  • Lymphocyte → Responsible for immune responses.

  • Macrophage → Performs phagocytosis and antigen presentation.

High-yield histology recall:

Neutral fat storage cell = Adipocyte
Antibody production = Plasma cell
Phagocytosis = Macrophage

Exam pearl:
Fat-storing cell of connective tissue = Adipocyte.

Anatomy-01.question: ৩৫) Major location of Langerhans cell is
৩৬) Which type of fibre is abundant in immune system?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is reticular fibre. Reticular fibres form a delicate supporting network (stroma) in lymphoid organs, which is essential for immune cell organization.

Key locations:

  • Lymph nodes

  • Spleen

  • Bone marrow

  • Other lymphoid tissues

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Collagen → Provides tensile strength and is abundant in connective tissues, but not the main supporting fibre of immune organs.

  • Elastic → Provides elasticity in tissues like large arteries, lungs, and skin.

  • All of them → Reticular fibres are specifically abundant in lymphoid organs.

High-yield histology recall:

Immune system framework = Reticular fibres (Type III collagen)
Tendon = Type I collagen
Elastic tissues = Elastic fibres

Exam pearl:
Lymphoid organs are supported by reticular fibre network.

৪৪) Biaxial joint
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is wrist. The wrist (radiocarpal) joint is a biaxial synovial joint of the condyloid (ellipsoid) type, allowing movement in two axes.

Movements:

  • Flexion and extension

  • Abduction and adduction

  • Circumduction (combination)

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Elbow → Uniaxial hinge joint.

  • Hip → Multiaxial ball-and-socket joint.

  • Shoulder → Multiaxial ball-and-socket joint.

High-yield anatomy recall:

Biaxial synovial joint → Wrist (condyloid), thumb CMC (saddle)
Uniaxial → Elbow, interphalangeal joints
Multiaxial → Hip, shoulder

Exam pearl:
Radiocarpal joint = Biaxial condyloid joint.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৫) Cristae is a characteristic of
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is mitochondria. Cristae are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane that increase surface area for oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production.

Key points:

  • Cristae → Inner mitochondrial membrane

  • Function:

    • Increase surface area

    • Site of electron transport chain

    • ATP synthesis by ATP synthase

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Golgi apparatus → Has flattened cisternae; involved in packaging and modification.

  • Lysosome → Contains hydrolytic enzymes for intracellular digestion.

  • Ribosome → Site of protein synthesis.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Cristae → Mitochondria → ATP production
Cisternae → Golgi apparatus / ER

Exam pearl:
Folds of inner mitochondrial membrane = Cristae.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৬) Thickness of cell membrane
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is 4.5–10 nm. The plasma membrane thickness is approximately 4.5–10 nanometres (nm), with an average of about 7.5 nm.

Key points:

  • Plasma membrane structure:

    • Phospholipid bilayer

    • Embedded proteins

    • Carbohydrate components

  • Thickness varies depending on cell type and membrane composition.

The other options are incorrect because:

  • 5.5–10 nm, 6.5–10 nm, 7.5–10 nm → These represent narrower ranges and are not the standard accepted range.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Plasma membrane thickness = 4.5–10 nm
Structure = Phospholipid bilayer + proteins

Exam pearl:
Average plasma membrane thickness ≈ 7.5 nm.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৭) Cytoskeleton of a cell are –
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is microtubules. Microtubules are one of the major components of the cytoskeleton, providing structural support and helping in intracellular transport.

Components of cytoskeleton:

  • Microtubules ✓

  • Microfilaments (actin)

  • Intermediate filaments

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Mitochondria → Membrane-bound organelle responsible for ATP production.

  • Centrosome → Organizes microtubules but is not itself a cytoskeletal component.

  • Ribosome → Non-membranous organelle involved in protein synthesis.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Cytoskeleton = Microtubules + Microfilaments + Intermediate filaments

Exam pearl:
Microtubules are a major cytoskeletal component.

Anatomy-01.question: ৪৯) Posttranslational modifications of proteins take place in-
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is Golgi complex. Golgi apparatus performs important post-translational modifications of proteins, including glycosylation, phosphorylation, and sorting before transport to their final destination.

Key points:

  • Golgi complex functions:

    • Protein modification ✓

    • Glycosylation ✓

    • Packaging and sorting ✓

    • Formation of secretory vesicles ✓

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum → Site of initial protein synthesis and early modifications (e.g., folding, disulfide bond formation).

  • Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum → Lipid synthesis and detoxification.

  • Nucleus → DNA replication and transcription.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Rough ER → Protein synthesis + initial processing
Golgi apparatus → Post-translational modification + packaging

Exam pearl:
Major post-translational protein modification site = Golgi complex.

Anatomy-01.question: ৫০) Which one is not the components of nucleus?
Anatomy-01.exp:
The correct answer is ribosome. Ribosomes are not components of the nucleus; they are non-membranous organelles involved in protein synthesis in the cytoplasm (and attached to rough ER).

Components of nucleus:

  • Nuclear membrane (nuclear envelope) ✓

  • Nucleoplasm ✓

  • Chromatin ✓

  • Nucleolus ✓

The other options are incorrect because:

  • Nuclear membrane → Outer boundary of nucleus.

  • Nucleoplasm → Internal fluid matrix of nucleus.

  • Chromatin → DNA-protein complex containing genetic material.

High-yield cell biology recall:

Nucleus = Nuclear membrane + Nucleoplasm + Chromatin + Nucleolus
Ribosome = Protein synthesis (cytoplasm/RER)

Exam pearl:
Ribosome is not a component of the nucleus.
